questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The academic aspect of exploring a country, where the school system differed from the Danish way of teaching and also differed in what was being teached. Also, I was really interested in experiencing the american culture more in depth rather than just what you could learn from a 3 weeks holiday there. I feel that the american culture is something which most be experienced through living in the country for a longer time to also be able to meet people and learn about their impressions of their own country. Furthermore I chose Seattle do to its placing in Washington State by the pacific northwest and its beautiful surrounding nature which was perfect for hiking and skiing combined with a vibrant city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to get into the country and the visa proces after arriving at the airport was much less frightening than I had imagined. I had a family friend, who I lived with for the first 2 weeks, so he picked me up and showed me everything I needed to know, therefor I don't really know how easy it is to find information, if you don't know anybody in the country beforehand.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was introduction days at the university three days before school started, which was a helpful way of getting to know the university, which is very big compared to CSS. They also had an orientation day for all the new international students, where they told os all the relevant information regarding how to sign up for classes, what we needed to know about health insurance, who to contact regarding this and that and so on, which was very helpful. But still, it is a very big institution and there were still, after does days and in the beginning of the first quarter, a lot of things we didn't know about, that we learnt along the way

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I would definitly recommend to rent an airbnb for the first days or first week or two when arriving and wait to find housing until you are there. It was very easy to find housing through the facebook site "UW - housing, apartments and sublets". I made a post together with my friend that we were searching for housing, and then different people reached out to us regarding that they were looking for roommates. It was nicer to be able to see the area and the apartment and roommates before saying yes to anything + there is also a lot of scammers, that you should be aware of which is just easier if you can meet with them in person.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in the area called "U district" which is not on campus but 5 minutes away from campus and the lecture halls. This was very convenient, since I could walk to classes in 5-10 minutes from my apartment. But in this area there are also a lot of homeless people who are very high on drugs and I felt unsafe walking around in the area at night time when it was dark, I even got chased by a man with a machette knife one night right out in front of my apartment building. So even though it is convienient, I would choose differently another time and choose neighborhoods further away from campus, where I would feel more safe + closer to other activities or nature parks that wasn't just campus such as Revenna, Capitol Hill, Freemont or Ballard. Revenna is with in walking distance to the school and I would say one of the safest neighborhoods in Seattle. Capitol Hill is the furtherest away, but very easy to get to by train, which stops right by campus. Ballard is far away and takes 40 minutes to get to by bus, but it is a very, very cozy and calm area with beautiful parks and nice shops and bars and restaurants!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Course registration opened to students to months before school started and therefor also 1.5 months before I got to the college. I found the online proces of registrering very difficult, since you had to show that you had the right prerequisites to be able to take courses higher than level 100-200, since they didn't know your prerequisites as an international student. This meant, that I had to write to each professor and ask, if I could take their course, and often times I could not. But then when I arrived at the university and could talk to the professors myself everything was much easier. So therefor I didn't sign up for any classes besides one before I arrived. This also meant, that a lot of the classes that I wanted was already filled up, unfortunately.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had an online zoom-session with the psychology department and their study guide before I arrived, because I was a little stressed about waiting to sign up for courses. They were really helpfull and gave me names of different people I could reach out to to get further help, which was a big help. They were also my primary contact when I had to register when I came to the country

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Semi - I got some classes, but unfortunately there was also a lot of classes that I would have preferred that I couldn't do to either the classes being sparred for national, american students only or because classes were already full when I got there.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep calm and be patient in the proces of registrating for classes. It takes time, and there isn't much you can do before you arrive in the country, where you can meet with people in person and get help. So even though I was a little stressed about not having signed up for classes before I arrived, I ended up getting some interesting courses that I was happy about.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The levels were lower than in Denmark, I would say. There is much more day-to-day work than I have been used to from Denmark, so I spent a lot more time on homeworks, but the level of these assignments wasn't that high, and they only read secondary texts and textbooks, which also meant that the level of the reading wasn't that difficult. Also, I had no final exams in any of my courses since they grade you through out the quarter, so you get a combined grate in the end, which meant, that I didn't have a stressed exam period as I normally would have in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was much more personal with a lot of back and forth between the teacher and the students, and often we also as students had to teach each other in what we had read for todays class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Health disparities, SOC 390, introduction to human strategic resource management

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked health disparities

questions.answer: Food was really, really expensive, especially if you wanted to eat healthy and wanted fresh vegetables. A fresh bell pepper could cost up to 28 DKK for one.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Not much, everything was pretty much more expensive than I had expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had very could sports facilities, such as a great gym with a pool and a bouldering hall. You could also take yoga classes, pilates, basket and much more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking!! The nature around seattle and in Washington state in general is so beautiful, especially in the fall. Also they have great techno clubs, and capitol Hill is in general a very cool area with great thrift shops and cafe, and they love sunday morning drag brunches and drag shows at night. This area also have the best clubs, especially queer and techno clubs. I would also recommend the bouldering hall in Freemont, freemont sunday market and the ballard area! And then look up restaurants in the city, they have a very good culinary scene in Seattle that isn't too expensive.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking!! The nature around seattle and in Washington state in general is so beautiful, especially in the fall. Also they have great techno clubs, and capitol Hill is in general a very cool area with great thrift shops and cafe, and they love sunday morning drag brunches and drag shows at night. This area also have the best clubs, especially queer and techno clubs. I would also recommend the bouldering hall in Freemont, freemont sunday market and the ballard area! And then look up restaurants in the city, they have a very good culinary scene in Seattle that isn't too expensive

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy since the american culture is so engrained in the danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That they don't really speak more in depth with each other - it is difficult to really get to know americans, since a lot of the conversations mainly are more "superficial"

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That they are a very friendly culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't find housing before you arrive and don't live on campus - especially not if you are a little older than 19-21 years old, which is the mean age at cmapus I would say 
Be patient when it comes to signing up for courses 
Safe up money! It was much more expensive to live there than I imagined

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No :))

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting other people and experiencing a new culture and country as well as having a lot of time for myself, which I don't really have in Denmark in the same way, since you have work, studies and friends and families back home. You have a lot more time for yourself, where you completly choose for yourself, what you want to do, which to me was a kind of unique experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Money and feeling safe

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
